config_name: Dell Plus 16 2-in-1 — Core Ultra 5 226V, 16GB LPDDR5X, 512GB SSD, 16" touch (Home)

specs.keyboard_notes: Full numpad, shallow mushy keys, non-haptic trackpad

battery.notes: 64Wh, low-power Ultra 5 226V; ~6.5-7h real mixed use by CNET anchor calibration.

price.notes: VERIFIED BBY 19270349 $1,299.95 (no discount). Refurb twin 19612837 $1,034.95. Cheapest new 16" 2-in-1 at CA retail.

offers.name: Dell Plus 16" Touchscreen 2-in-1 Laptop - Intel Core Ultra 5-226V - 16GB LPDDR5X - 512GB SSD - Windows 11 Home - Ice Blue

reviews.quote: there are a few too many minuses to give this Plus a full-throated recommendation.

praises: $1,300 for a brand-new 16-inch touch convertible — cheapest big-screen 2-in-1 at CA retail
Lunar Lake Ultra 5 is still quick for browsing/Office and very power-efficient
Copilot+ NPU (40+ TOPS) at a budget price
Sturdy chassis, understated Ice Blue look
Full numpad and generous touch panel for movies/tent mode
complaints: Base 226V iGPU is weaker than Arc 140V — casual gaming only
512GB soldered-class storage with no upgrade path
Same mushy keyboard and down-firing muffled speakers as the rest of the line
Battery ~7h real-world; 2.0 kg weight for a convertible
1200p on 16" is visibly coarse for text

design_philosophy: The entry door to Dell's rebranded mid-tier consumer convertibles: same DB06250 chassis and Lunar Lake platform as the higher tiers, but with the slowest chip and half the storage, priced to undercut every other 16-inch 2-in-1 on the shelf.
rating_notes: Inferred from CNET DB06250 anchor (SHARED-dell-2in1.md): Ultra 5 226V vs 258V = -1 gaming (basic Lunar Lake iGPU, no Arc 140V), -0.5 productivity; 16" 1200p IPS screen_quality 5.0 per anchor. No direct pro review of this tier.
